jobs.description: Employer: LearnWell Expires: 10/25/2026 At LearnWell, we are committed to changing the lives of the 10 million students in the U.S. who are dealing with behavioral health issues. For more than 26 years, we have provided on-site educational services in hospitals, helping these school-age patients continue their education during treatment and reintegrate successfully into the classroom. With a network of over 200 educators, we strive to make a positive impact for generations to come.We are currently seeking passionate and creative teachers to join our growing team in the areas of Westchester, Suffolk, and Bronx county, including Briarcliff Manor, Amityville, & White Plains. These unique positions will involve working in a fast-paced behavioral health facility, providing academic support to school-age patients in a small classroom setting as they receive treatment.In this role, you will have the opportunity to plan and deliver daily lesson plans, provide individualized assistance to students, and regularly communicate about student progress as needed. Additionally, you will monitor and adjust teaching strategies to ensure student success and maintain accurate attendance and session reports. Most of our class sizes range from 8 to 15 school-age patients at any one time.We offer a very generous package of paid time off including vacation time, sick time, federal holidays, and paid school breaks. We also offer healthcare benefits that include medical, dental, and vision. Additional benefits include paid family leave options, 401K, employer sponsored life insurance policies, and annual grants for tuition reimbursement.Join our team and make a meaningful impact while enjoying competitive pay, benefits, and supportive work environments!Position Highlights:Part Time White Plains Teacher: 10 months, 12:00-4:00pm. Teaching adolescent ages 14-17. Inpatient eating-disorder treatment setting.Part Time Briarcliff Manor Teacher: 12 months, 8:00-12:00pm. Teaching adolescent ages 12-17. Residential eating-disorder treatment setting.Part Time Bronx Teacher: 10 months, 8:00-12:00pm. Teaching adolescent ages 12-17. Partial hospitalization day treatment program setting.Full Time Amityville Teacher: 10 months, 7:30-4:00pm. Teaching adolescent ages 12-17. Teachers prioritize student school assignments provided, and use LearnWell's library of lessons and resources to supplement student work.Qualifications:B.A/B.S degree from an accredited institutionNew York State Teaching CertificationComfort working within a pediatric and adolescent populationReliable TransportationJoin LearnWell as we strive to make a difference in the lives of students with behavioral health needs. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.title: Tissue Family Services Coordinator at Infinite Legacy
jobs.description: Employer: Infinite Legacy Expires: 10/25/2026 General Job Summary:Under the general direction of the Regional Clinical Manager, Family Services - Tissue, the Tissue Family Services Coordinator 1 (TFSC 1) is responsible for coordinating a wide range of support for potential tissue/eye donor families. Information is to be articulated in an easily understood and accurate manner to families whose ability to process information is impaired by emotionally traumatic circumstances. Infinite Legacy’s Tissue Family Services Coordinator 1 coordinates and facilitates emotional support during and after the discussion of the donation process. Rapport is established with donor families, Infinite Legacy team members, and hospital staff involved in the donation process. The Tissue FSC I will be aware and sensitive to diversity of all kinds (cultural, religious, educational, etc.) while working with families and hospital staff.Please note: This is a fully remote position. Applicants must reside within our designated service area (Washington, DC, Maryland, or Northern Virginia). Applicants with OPO experience outside of our DSA may also be considered. Occasional travel may be required for meetings, training, or company events. Education and Experience:Master’s degree at an accredited college or university in social work, counseling, psychology, nursing, or related degree. Bachelor’s degree will be considered if relevant experience is met.1- 2 years’ experience in an acute health care setting (preferred), hospice, bereavement counseling center, crisis intervention, etc. where there was active involvement in issues involving death, dying, grief and loss. Required Skills/Abilities: Ability to interact with grieving families in a supportive, empathic manner while taking into consideration actual or potential cultural diversities.Ability to communicate effectively, verbally and in writing to provide information to donor families, recipients, health care personnel and the general public.Ability to comfortably use technology to access and utilize Infinite Legacy databases, draft letters, send/receive email, and access the Internet for vital information/resources to assist donor families. Must have the ability to connect to the Internet safely with speeds capable of supporting both a VoIP phone and laptop. The requirements for such can change at any time and the user must be able to able to maintain current technologies. Must be highly accountable and able to work autonomously. Must possess a high level of self-motivation and well-developed time management, organizational, and problem-solving skills.Tissue FSCs will do twelve 12-hour shifts per month in addition to simulation time with both external and internal partners, team, and organizational meetings. Duties/Responsibilities:The Tissue FSC I will establish initial contact over the phone with the potential donor family and offer the option of tissue and eye donation in accordance with all state, federal and industry related regulations. Provides the family with a copy of an authorization or disclosure, Document of Gift if applicable and completes the medical/social history proficiently.The Tissue FSC I will provide trauma, grief, and bereavement support services for the family over the phone during initial contact. Tissue FSC I will identify if additional support is needed and connect the family with local hospital or community resources to provide additional support. In addition, the plans for grief and bereavement services will be communicated to the Aftercare Team at Infinite Legacy who is responsible for following the donor family after donation. Completes all necessary documentation within the time limits established by Infinite Legacy and its regulatory bodies. Collaborates with local funeral homes and whole-body donation programs to ensure that the donor family is supported, and the funeral home or whole-body donation program is aware of the tissue recovery process.Works in conjunction with appropriate Infinite Legacy staff during local tissue and eye cases. Collaborates closely with clinical personnel, DSC, Tissue AOC, HS, and TR during donor management to ensure that donor families’ needs are communicated to the Infinite Legacy team in addition to ensuring all case logistics are being communicated effectively to support donor and family needs during the donation process. Triages phone calls from families that are received from the Donor Services Center as it pertains to tissue donation needs, hospice referrals and medical evaluation for donation. At times collaboration with Hospice RNs, Nursing Homes or Assisted Living Facilities are needed to ensure the donors wishes can be honored.Navigates sensitive conversations as it pertains to the rejection of tissues post donation process. Initiates follow-up support over the phone to donor families as it relates to offering donor in spirit post donation should tissues be rejected or not able to be transplanted. Facilitates communication with outside OPO’s who require local registry checks within IL’s DSA. This includes DC, VA, and MD registry checks in a timely manner. Initiates follow-up support to donor and non-donor families when appropriate and is responsible for ensuring effective communication and documentation of aftercare components within the time limits established by Infinite Legacy and its regulatory bodies.Participates in continuing education as identified by the Family Services Manager – Tissue. jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: USA TODAY Election Night Reporter at USA Today - Election Team
jobs.description: Employer: USA Today - Election Team Expires: 10/25/2026 USA TODAY is currently recruiting election-night Reporters across Wyoming for the 2026 General Election on November 3rd. Reporters will visit a local polling place or County office and report unofficial election night results to USA TODAY as they are released. This is a paid, nonpartisan role focused solely on collecting and transmitting official election results quickly and accurately. It is a great opportunity to participate in the election process and help ensure timely reporting of results.Position Details- Locations: Available across the state (If you're interested we likely have a position available near you!)- Date: Tuesday, November 3, 2026- Hours: 7:45 pm until final results are released- Pay: Flat fee equal to $125 Responsibilities- Report official election results using a smartphone on our web-based reporting system- Remain on site to provide updates on result releases- Communicate with election officials as needed- Attend a brief mandatory training and rehearsal before Election Day that will cover how to report results, interact with election officials, and receive payment This position typically takes around 4 hours but could go longer, and Reporters should be prepared to stay until the election official indicates that no more results will be released that evening, or until your Coordinator dismisses you. The potential to become a regular election night Reporter is very high, so long as the job is done well. Requirements- Smartphone- Reliable transportation- Attention to detail and ability to report results quickly and accurately If interested, please email your name, phone number, and ZIP code to Ryan at rguistwite@usatodayco.com Candidates who also send a sentence or two about why they are interested and a good fit for the role will receive priority consideration.

jobs.title: Behavior Technician / RBT (Part-Time), ABA Therapy at Early Autism Solutions
jobs.description: Employer: Early Autism Solutions Expires: 10/25/2026 Behavior Technician / RBT (Part-Time), ABA TherapyJob type: JobEmployment type: Part-timeLocation: Washington, DC (school, home, and clinic-based sessions)Pay: $20–$25/hour, based on experience and certificationAbout Early Autism SolutionsEarly Autism Solutions (EAS) is a DC-based Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) practice founded in 2011. We provide individualized, evidence-based services to children with autism in schools, homes, and our office in Dupont Circle. Our team is led by Board Certified Behavior Analysts who give hands-on supervision and mentorship. jobs.title: School Psychologist/School Psychology Assistant at Wraparound Experts
jobs.description: Employer: Wraparound Experts Expires: 10/25/2026 Position: School Psychologist/School Psychologist Assistant Responsibilities will largely center on student assessment and evaluation, including the administration, scoring, and interpretation of standardized tests.Location: Cleveland, Ohio and Mentor, OhioVenue: Private school/Charter School settingsPosition Type: Full-Time and Part-Time opportunities availablePosition Details Are you interested in working as a School Psychologist within a private school or charter school setting? Wraparound Experts is currently accepting applicants for full-time and part-time positions. Locations include the East side of Cleveland and Mentor. Apply now to take advantage of this exciting opportunity!• Specific locations, caseloads, and positions will be discussed during the interview. • Start Date: ASAPWraparound Experts is proud to be recognized for our dedication to improving lives. We won the 2024 Real Leaders Impact Award - Most Valuable Mission. We also earned the Bell Seal (2024) and the Gold Bell Seal (2025 & 2026) for Workplace Mental Health from Mental Health America (MHA). In the Summer of 2025, we were a Going to Bat for Small Businesses recipient chosen by PNC Bank and the Cleveland Guardians. Finally, WE is proud to serve as the Mental Health Consultant for Head Start Programs in Cuyahoga and Summit Counties!Who We AreWraparound Experts (WE) is a trusted local partner for schools across Northeast Ohio, providing specialized services and educational staffing solutions to support children and families. We place Special Education and Mental Health professionals at elementary and secondary schools. WE is dedicated to connecting schools with licensed, qualified Experts who understand the ‘wraparound model’. Our staff goes above and beyond their traditional roles, working together effectively to coordinate services among teachers, support staff and other experts. By wrapping around students with support, we can achieve positive outcomes for students and their families, while fostering a positive work environment.Beyond staffing solutions, WE offers comprehensive behavioral and mental health training for children, families, and school staff throughout the year. We also provide specialized psychological testing services for autism, ADHD, and learning disabilities.Overall, our mission is to empower children to thrive mentally, emotionally, and academically. If you are dedicated to making a real, lasting change in the lives of children, then Wraparound Experts might be the place for you. Join us and be part of our mission to make a difference! Job SummaryThe School Psychologist will develop and provide comprehensive school psychological services to students, families, and schools in compliance with local, state, and federal laws. This broad range of services will meet the academic and mental health needs of students to which they are assigned. The School Psychologist will conduct the psycho-educational evaluations and assessments for students to determine educational needs and eligibility for special education services. The School Psychologist will work with parents, teachers, and other special education professionals to help design an individualized education plan (an IEP) that best fits the child’s situation. Overall, the School Psychologist will provide support and therapeutic services to students with diverse needs as prescribed by Wraparound Experts and the principal of the school. jobs.title: Classroom Guide at Elm City Montessori School
jobs.description: Employer: Elm City Montessori School Expires: 10/25/2026 Elm City Montessori SchoolElm City Montessori School, launched in August 2014, is New Haven's first public Montessori school. We are committed to actively building an Antibias Antiracist school community. We are seeking Classroom Guides to support us in building a vibrant and transformative learning environment in our growing school. We will serve 320 children preK-8th grade in the next academic year. New Haven, Connecticut is a thriving arts, cultural, and education hub, located in the center of a growing community of public Montessori schools.About the positionOur guides are fully trained Montessorians with an AMS or AMI diploma. Guides plan and prepare Montessori lessons across the curriculum, differentiating instruction to ensure growth for all students, collaborating with classroom, level, and school teams to plan curriculum, instruction, and assessment, partnering with families through regular communication to support children's growth, and participating in professional learning in social emotional skills, academics, and Anti-Bias Anti-Racist work. The Guide reports to the Principal, and works in collaboration with Classroom Assistant, SEL Team, and Coaches. This is a full time 10-Month with required August Training before the school year begins.Required QualificationsThis position requires certification to teach in the public schools in the State of CT and completion of a Montessori Training program. jobs.title: Program Director at Boys & Girls Club of Paterson and Passaic
jobs.description: Employer: Boys & Girls Club of Paterson and Passaic Expires: 10/25/2026 The mission of the Boys & Girls Club of Paterson and Passaic is to inspire and enable all young people, especially those that need us most, to realize their full potential as productive, responsible and caring citizens.The Boys & Girls Club of Paterson and Passaic offers a safe, wholesome after school environment for kids age 5 through 18 to have fun and learn. During summer months, a day camp is offered.Our professional staff and team of dedicated volunteers deliver a comprehensive array of high quality educational, social, and recreational programs.Role: Program DirectorReports To: Clubhouse DirectorType: Full-TimePOSITION SUMMARY:The Program Director supervises and manages the planning, organizing and conducting of programs, activities and events, providing individual guidance as needed in the Clubhouse. The Program Director implements and supports engaging and age-appropriate programs within the priority outcome areas of Academic Success, Healthy Lifestyles, Good Character, and Citizenship and demonstrates to staff how to incorporate youth development principles; provide guidance to club members and their families; and manage behaviors resulting in a safe and positive environment for youth. The Program Director also provides leadership and supervision to assigned program staff.ESSENTIAL JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:Under the direct supervision of the Clubhouse Director, the Program Director is responsible for carrying out staff and program supervision for Clubhouse after-school programs.Ensure a positive, healthy and safe environment for youth members and staff.Supervise the performance of assigned program staff and train on all Club Policies and Practices.Manage club staff hours, payroll administration and performance management issues.Maintain licensing requirements and documentation on-site to meet standards and protocols.Act as temporary coverage for the Clubhouse Director when needed.Participate in organizational meetings and conferences as required.Responsible for all program content and acquisition of program supplies and equipment.Conduct initial interviews on potential employees, and train program staff in compliance with NJ Bureau of Licensing standards.Maintain open lines of communication with direct supervisor and colleagues.Communicate any potential issue or concern regularly with Clubhouse Director or administrative staff regarding personnel, parent or Club members.Engage parents regarding opportunities and expectations of club members, as well as general club participation.Consult with parents concerning member behavior or personal issues.Promote and provide information to prospective families for enrollment.Communicate changes with staff and families regarding policies and procedures. jobs.feedName: Michael D. Eisner College of Education
jobs.title: Program Operations Intern - Civic Education at Cato Institute
jobs.description: Employer: Cato Institute Expires: 10/25/2026 To be considered for this role, you must apply directly through our online application. OverviewSphere Education Initiatives is a nonpartisan educator professional development program housed at the Cato Institute that provides teachers and administrators in grades 5–12 with viewpoint-diverse resources to strengthen free speech, civil discourse, and civic culture in their classrooms. Sphere's flagship program is Sphere Summit — a fully funded, five-day in-person event held twice each summer in Washington, DC — alongside Sphere on the Road (school and district visits), the Sphere Alumni Fellowship (a six-month program for Summit graduates), and an expanding library of curriculum resources, including lesson plans, toolkits, and multimedia content. The internship covers program operations, curriculum creation, and administrative duties. The workload is event-focused and logistically demanding during Summit season, shifting to content development and program support at other times. It is ideal for applicants interested in K–12 civics education and educator professional growth who are also dependable, organized, and comfortable with operational tasks — including inventory management, shipping coordination, and CRM maintenance — as well as more in-depth curriculum and program work.ResponsibilitiesAssist with the Sphere Summit application review and program development, including communicating with participants and handling logistical arrangements.Provide operational support for Sphere on the Road and other Sphere events, including preparing materials, shipping packages, and managing inventory using EZO.Maintain and update Sphere's educator contacts and program records in Salesforce, including list maintenance and record management.Develop curriculum resources for teachers of grades 5–12 that promote civil discussion, diverse viewpoints, and civic participation in the classroom.Assist with the Sphere Alumni Fellowship, including organizing events, conducting research, and managing program logistics.Assist in creating program materials, lookbooks, and other communications as assigned.Assist at Sphere Summit and other Cato events as needed, including participant support and on-site logistics.Required QualificationsStrong interest in K–12 civic education, civil discourse, and educator professional development; comfortable engaging respectfully and constructively with educators and participants from diverse viewpoints.Understanding of libertarian and classical-liberal thought and aligning with Cato's principles of individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace, while recognizing that Sphere's programs are explicitly nonpartisan and support educators across the political spectrum.Clear written and verbal communication; professional demeanor in participant-facing and vendor-facing interactions.Reliable follow-through in event-driven settings with changing priorities and strict logistics timelines.Professionalism, humility, and an entrepreneurial mindset — willingness to handle both substantive project work and operational responsibilities as needed.Professionalism, reliability, and attention to detail — this work requires accuracy in both data handling and written output, as well as consistent follow-through across operational and content tasks.Preferred QualificationsFamiliarity with Salesforce or a similar CRM for contact management, list hygiene, and basic reporting.Proficient in Microsoft Excel for list management and basic tracking.Prior experience in program administration, event coordination, or education-related work through a school, nonprofit, or civic organization.Knowledge of K–12 curriculum design or educational content development.The Cato Internship ProgramCato’s paid internships are available for undergraduates, recent graduates, graduate students, law students, and early-career professionals who are strongly committed to individual liberty, limited government, free markets, and peace—principles that together form libertarianism, also known as “classical liberalism,” “market liberalism,” or, to many of our international friends, simply “liberalism.” All Cato interns participate in the same intensive seminar series, which covers a wide range of topics in history, philosophy, policy, and professional development. Interns also assist with events and occasionally support Cato staff with other daily tasks. Interns receive competitive pay. Part-time roles are adjusted accordingly and require a minimum of 25 hours per week. Program participants must be able to attend in person in Washington, DC.For more information about the internship program and experience, we encourage you to explore our website. If you have any questions, email studentprograms@cato.org.

jobs.description: Employer: Norway Health Center Expires: 10/25/2026 We are a behavioral health clinic in the Twin Cities. Founded in 2020, our mission is to empower local community leaders (like yourself) to pioneer healthcare and community development to alleviate human suffering. Norway Health Center's core values are: 1. Mission First2. Be Pioneers3. Cultivate Comradery4. Pursue Excellence5. Build a Legacy We are launching a home-based EIDBI ABA program in Norway Health Center, supporting children and youth under the age of 21 with Autism Spectrum Disorder and developmental needs. We utilize positive reinforcement within an ABA framework to build skills, teach new abilities, and reduce behaviors that limit independence. Our goal is to strengthen families, promote inclusion, and provide high-quality, ethical services in the home and community. We value dignity, respect, and a supportive work environment where professionals can thrive.Job Description: We are seeking a compassionate and dedicated EIDBI Level 2 Provider to join our growing team. Responsibilities:Provide 1:1 ABA-based intervention in the home and community, following treatment goals and strategies outlined in the Individual Treatment Plan (ITP).Support skill development in ongoing treatment planning.Collaborate with families and caregivers to promote skill generalization in natural routines and daily activities.Participate in supervision, coaching, and required training to ensure fidelity to ABA methods and EIDBI guidelines.Utilize crisis management techniques when necessary to maintain safety and uphold best practices.Maintain timely and accurate documentation and follow all professional, ethical, and program standards.Complete all mandated trainings per DHS/EIDBI guidelines prior to working with clients and throughout employment.Qualifications:Minimum Qualifications: To qualify for this position, candidates must be at least 18 years old, and meet one of the following qualification pathways: Bachelor’s Degree Pathway:Bachelor’s degree in behavioral health, child development, or a related field AND one of the following:– At least 1,000 hours of clinical experience or training with individuals with ASD or related conditions; OR– Equivalent graduate-level coursework in ASD, treatment strategies, or child development; OR– Certification as a BCaBA, RBT, or in another DHS-recognized treatment modality.Associate’s Degree Pathway:Associate’s degree in behavioral health, child development, or a related field AND at least 2,000 hours of supervised clinical experience providing treatment to individuals with ASD or related conditions.Experience-Only Pathway:At least 4,000 hours of supervised clinical experience delivering treatment to individuals with ASD or related conditions.Graduate Student Pathway:Currently enrolled in a graduate program in a behavioral health or related field AND formally assigned to an EIDBI provider agency for clinical training under a Qualified Supervising Professional (QSP).Language/Cultural Provider Pathway:Fluent in a non-English language or certified by a tribal government, has completed required EIDBI trainings, AND receives weekly supervision until 1,000 supervised clinical hours are met.Bachelor’s-in-Progress Pathway:Currently enrolled in or recently completed a bachelor’s degree in a behavioral health or related field, AND receives twice-monthly supervision until 1,000 supervised clinical hours are met.Treatment Modality Pathway:Completed initial certification in the agency’s treatment modality, completed EIDBI required trainings, AND receives weekly supervision until 1,000 supervised clinical hours are met.Must provide sufficient documentation to verify eligibility as an EIDBI Level 2 provider.Experience working with children with autism or developmental disabilities is preferred.Strong interpersonal and communication skills.Empathy, patience, and the ability to build rapport with clients.Be able to pass a criminal background check.Valid driver's license.Reliable transportation and carry own vehicle insurance.Ability to work independently and as part of a team.Flexibility in working hours to accommodate client schedules.Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.Hours:Job Type: Part-time / Full-timeFlexible hours between 7:00am and 8:00 pm, depending on patient availability.Schedules are up to 40 hours per week, typically Monday through Friday, with flexibilityBenefits:Competitive salary; $20 to $27 per hour depending on experience.Paid Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) training, supervision, and examination feesComprehensive health benefits (Medical, Dental and Vision)401(k) retirement plan with up to 3.0% employer matchTravel time reimbursementPaid time off (PTO)Extensive new hire training; Opportunities for professional growth and career advancementFlexible full-time and part-time schedules (You create your own schedule) Available Employment Type: W-2 Work Setting:Hybrid: Office and Client’s Home (Community-Based Setting) Location: St Paul, MN 55130

jobs.title: Swim, Boating or Waterski Specialist at Camp IHC
jobs.description: Employer: Camp IHC - Camp IHC Expires: 10/25/2026 Make a SPLASH on the water this summer!At Camp IHC our waterfront family is broken down into three areas. Swim coaching and lifeguarding, boating, and waterskiing and wakeboarding.Every day of summer camp you will find campers and counselors having a crazy amount of fun in the pool or on the lake. Our Swim Staff are headed up by our waterfront directors, they will bring your lifeguarding, coaching and instruction skills to the next level through an extensive pre-camp training program. Boating takes place on our beautiful 35 acre, spring fed natural lake and there’s no better way to spend your summer days than Kayaking, Canoeing and Stand Up Paddle Boarding. The boating team consists of 6-8 staff. As a boating instructor you are responsible for teaching campers the basics skills associated with Kayaking, Canoeing and Stand Up Paddle Boarding all while having an amazing time on the lake. As Campers play, your ultimate goal is to keep them safe and make sure they are having fun!Waterski is one of the coolest areas on camp. Every camper and counselor can’t wait until it’s their turn to go to the waterski dock for an activity period.As part of the waterski team you will take campers waterskiing, tubing, wake-boarding and kneeboarding. At Camp IHC the Waterski instructors will teach around 7 periods a day. You’ll help teach campers from 6-16 years old with a variety of abilities.If all of that sounds amazing to you let me make make it even better. You can use this experience as an INTERNSHIP as well! So what are you waiting for? Your summer home awaits.

jobs.title: Homeschool Tutor at Lark Rise Hall
jobs.description: Employer: Lark Rise Hall Expires: 10/25/2026 Tutoring Job OpportunityWe are hiring motivated, patient, and passionate tutors to work at our homeschool tutoring hall.Lark Rise Hall is a 501c3 nonprofit organization, registered with the state. We have enrolled over 30 students for this year, and have rented out the beautiful Bullock Room in the Provo City Library.The job would be to assist the students (ages 6-12) as they work through their own math curriculums they bring from home, as well as assisting with language arts curriculums and writing. We plan to have one tutor per every three students so individual needs can be seen and met.Our program runs from September 1, 2026, to April 29, 2027. Class will be held from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m, on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday, with breaks around holidays. There are also a few days in the year when the library will not be available and we will not meet on those days.Interested tutors could apply to work Tuesday, or Wednesday, or Thursday, or all three days.A few more details:—Starting pay will be $14/hr.—Tutors will be expected to wear business or business casual clothing to tutor in each day—Tutors will be hired as independent contractors, ready to bring their tutoring skills to the table—Tutors should feel confident that they can walk a student through elementary math and language arts lessons, as well as writing practice. Students working in curriculums for 4th grade and higher will be askedto bring an answer key for their tutor to reference.—Each tutor will split time between three students they will help throughout the day (time breakdowns are detailed out on the website under the Schedule tab). Applicants can apply by emailing a resume and brief cover letter to info@larkrisehall.org . We will bereceiving applications and holding interviews from now until the positions are filled.Feel free to email info@larkrisehall.org with any questions beyond what has been described. We hope this will be an opportunity for interested individuals to earn some money while also gaining valuable tutoring experience.Thank you,Judy SorensonLark Rise Hall Chairinfo@larkrisehall.org

jobs.description: Employer: Santa Clara University Expires: 10/25/2026 Director, Center for Latine Theology and Ministry Position Title:Director, Center for Latine Theology and MinistryPosition Type:RegularHiring Range:$102,800.00 - $128,560.00; Compensation will be based on education, experience, skills relevant to the role, and internal equity.Pay Frequency:AnnualA. POSITION PURPOSEUnder the supervision of the Sr. Assistant Dean / Chief Operating Officer of the Jesuit School of Theology at Santa Clara University (JST-SCU), the Director will provide vision, strategic leadership, and administrative oversight for the Center for Latine Theology and Ministry (CLTM). The director will oversee the development, implementation, and sustainability of academic programs, ministerial formation, scholarly research, and community outreach initiatives that serve Latine pastoral leaders and communities.Towards this end, the Director will contribute to the strategic implementation of SCU's recent $10 Million Lilly Endowment Large-Scale Collaboration Grant (https://www.scu.edu/jst/news-and-events/stories/santa-clara-universitys-jesuit-school-of-theology-receives-10-million-grant-to-expand-and-strengthen-pastorally-engaged-catholic-theology-and-ministry.html). This will be done in coordination with the creation and launch of the Pope Francis Institute for Pastoral Flourishing (PFI), which integrates the work of the Jesuit School of Theology (JST), the Graduate Program in Pastoral Ministries (GPPM), and the Department of Religious Studies. The Director will play a vital leadership role in establishing Santa Clara University as a primary national hub for Latine theology and ministry. Informed by JST-SCU's strategic plan, En Camino, and Santa Clara University's Santa Clara Impact 2030, the Director will guide the Center through its integration into Santa Clara's Mission campus and foster strategic collaboration across university programs.B. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES1. Strategic Leadership - Lead the implementation of the strategic vision set forth for the Center for Latino Theology and Ministry in the $10M Lilly Endowment Large-Scale Collaboration Grant, positioning Santa Clara University as a primary national hub for Latine theology and ministry.- Align the work of the Center for Latine Theology and Ministry with the overall vision of the Pope Francis Institute for Pastoral Flourishing (PFI). This will entail a year of co-design that aligns and integrates programs and initiatives between the Jesuit School of Theology, the Graduate Program in Pastoral Ministries, and the Department of Religious Studies.- Provide overall vision and strategic direction for the CLTMin alignment with JST-SCU's mission and strategic goals.- Oversee the strategic planning, growth, and continuous quality improvement of non-degree and continuing education programs, including the Instituto Hispano.- Collaborate with administrators and faculty across the university leadership, faculty, and academic programs to integrate Latine theological perspectives and ministerial formation into broader academic offerings. 2. Academic Research Support - Promote and support academic research and scholarship focused on U.S. Latine theology, religiosidad popular, intercultural ministry, and contextual pastoral praxis.- Work towards establishing the CLTM as a hub for transdisciplinary research, bridging academic theological reflection with practical ministerial formation.- Convene symposia, academic lectures, and research initiatives that leverage Santa Clara University's robust cohort of Latine faculty (in the JST, GPPM, and Department of Religious Studies), who do work in U.S. Latine theology and ministry- Advance key priorities and themes articulated in the National Pastoral Plan for Hispanic/Latino Ministry and the V Encuentro through scholarly output and pastoral partnerships. 3. Network Building & Strategic Partnerships - Formalize and manage strategic academic and pastoral partnerships with national organizations, including the Academy of Catholic Hispanic Theologians of the United States (ACHTUS), to advance scholarly research, mentorship, and leadership formation.- Partner with external regional organizations such as RECOSS (Red de Educación Continua del Sur de California) and Iskali to expand young adult leadership initiatives, mentorship, and community-of-practice programs (acompañamiento).- Cultivate and sustain strong collaborative relationships with diocesan leaders, pastoral institutes, Catholic organizations, and community partners across the West Coast and nationally.- Lead and support advisory bodies, including local and regional pastoral partner councils, to ensure program offerings remain responsive to community needs.- Represent SCU and the Center at national conferences, academic symposia, and ministerial gatherings.- Develop initiatives to identify future Latine leaders and help them discern a degree in theological or pastoral studies 4. Grant Administration & Resource Development - Oversee the administration, execution, and reporting for grants awarded directly to or specifically supporting the CLTM- Lilly LSC Integration & Input: Serve as a key contributor and subject-matter expert for the Lilly Endowment Large-Scale Collaboration (LSC) Grant by providing accurate program data, metrics, and progress updates to the dedicated LSC Project Manager, who manages centralized grant reporting.- Resource Development & Sustainability: In collaboration with University Development, identify external funding opportunities, assist in cultivating donors, and draft grant proposals to ensure the long-term sustainability and expansion of CLTM initiatives.- Budget Oversight: Monitor center-specific budget allocations, program revenue (including Instituto Hispano revenue), and match funding commitments in coordination with the Dean's Office and JST Finance. 5. Operational & Personnel Management - Supervise, mentor, and evaluate CLTM administrative staff, including the Instituto Hispano Program Coordinator, project staff, and graduate student assistants.- Direct day-to-day operations of the Center, ensuring efficient administrative processes, event execution, and participant support.- Oversee marketing, outreach, and communications strategies to promote Center activities and engage prospective students. 6. Other duties as assigned in support of JST's mission and operational needsC. PROVIDES WORK DIRECTIONDirectly supervises professional staff (e.g., Instituto Hispano Program Coordinator), grant-funded staff, and graduate assistants.D. GENERAL GUIDELINESRecommends initiatives and implements changes to improve quality and services.Identifies and determines cause of problems; develops and presents recommendations for improvement of established processes and practices.Maintains contact with partners, community leaders, and students to solicit feedback for improved services.Maximizes productivity through use of appropriate tools, planned training, and performance initiatives.Researches and develops resources that create timely and efficient workflow.Prepares progress reports; informs supervisor of project status and deviation from grant or program goals.Ensures completeness, accuracy, and timeliness of all operational and grant-related functions.Prepares and submits grant and institutional reports as requested and required.Develops and implements guidelines to support the functions of the unit.E. QUALIFICATIONSThis position requires the ability to establish and maintain effective and cooperative working relationships within a diverse multicultural environment. Professional qualifications include the following:1. Scholarly and Professional Expertise - Deep knowledge of Latine theology and ministerial formation, and the ways in which they connect to the pastoral realities of Latine communities in the United States.- Strong understanding of the values, ideals, and mission of the Jesuit School of Theology and Jesuit higher education, more broadly.- Knowledge of ATS-accredited graduate theological education and non-degree certificate program structures. 2. Skills - Exceptional written and oral communication skills in both English and Spanish (bilingual fluency required).- Strong project management and organizational skills with sharp attention to detail.- Proven leadership and interpersonal skills in managing staff, building teams, and facilitating advisory groups.- Familiarity with grant management processes, grant reporting standards, and budget administration. 3. Abilities - Ability to engage, collaborate, and build trust with diverse stakeholders, including bishops, diocesan personnel, grassroots pastoral leaders, and faculty.- Ability to manage grant budgets, track metrics, and meet formal reporting deadlines.- Ability to navigate organizational transitions and lead strategic program growth.- Ability to exercise sound judgment, discretion, and maintain confidentiality. 4. EducationPh.D., D.Min., or equivalent doctorate preferred; Master's degree in Theology, Pastoral Ministry, Divinity, or a closely related field required.5. Years of Experience - Four or more years of progressively responsible administrative, leadership, or educational experience in a university, theological seminary, or pastoral organization. Experience managing grant-funded programs strongly preferred. F. PHYSICAL DEMANDSThe physical demands described below are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. G. WORK ENVIRONMENTJST-SCU allows employees to submit requests for Flexible and Remote work schedules as described in Policy 307 of the SCU employee handbook. If a remote schedule is approved, the school's standard is that all permanent employees work in person at least 60% of the time. Currently, this position is based at the JST-SCU campus in Berkeley, California. Beginning in Fall 2027, the position will be based at the school's location on Santa Clara University's main campus in Santa Clara, California. - Typical office environment.- Mostly indoor office environment with windows.- Offices with equipment noise and frequent interruptions. This is an initial 3-year fixed-term position, with potential for extension dependent on project milestones, performance, and funding allocation.TelecommuteSanta Clara University is registered to do business in the following states: California, Nevada, Oregon, Washington, Arizona, and Illinois. Employees approved to telecommute are required to perform their work within one of these states.EEO StatementEqual Opportunity/Notice of NondiscriminationSanta Clara University is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.title: Behavioral Technician at Bright Minds Developmental Center
jobs.description: Employer: Bright Minds Developmental Center Expires: 10/25/2026 Company DescriptionBright Minds Developmental Center is dedicated to helping individuals build confidence, develop independence, and thrive in their daily environments. We provide individualized support through adaptive and life skills training, social skills development, and parent training. Our services emphasize practical, real-world skills that promote greater independence at home and in the community, including communication, self-management, and community engagement. Bright Minds collaborates closely with families and multidisciplinary teams to deliver coordinated, compassionate, and sustainable support. Through hands-on learning and personalized care, we empower individuals to work toward a brighter, more independent future. Role DescriptionThe Behavioral Technician is a part-time, community-based position serving the San Fernando Valley and surrounding areas. This role involves implementing individualized behavior intervention plans under the supervision of a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) or clinical supervisor. Day-to-day responsibilities include providing direct 1:1 support to individuals, teaching adaptive and life skills, facilitating social skills development, and collecting accurate data on behaviors and progress. Behavioral Technicians collaborate with families and multidisciplinary team members, participate in team meetings, and maintain clear, professional documentation. The role also includes supporting parent training sessions, following safety protocols, and contributing to a positive, inclusive, and person-centered environment. LocationThis is a community-based, on-site position serving clients throughout the San Fernando Valley and surrounding areas, including Woodland Hills, Sherman Oaks, Calabasas, and Santa Clarita. Behavioral Technicians travel to client homes and community settings based on assigned cases and scheduling needs. QualificationsFoundational knowledge of Behavior Analysis and Applied Behavior Analysis, with the ability to implement behavior support plans consistently.Strong communication skills for interacting professionally with individuals, families, supervisors, and multidisciplinary team members, including clear documentation and reporting.Experience or training in behavioral intervention, including de-escalation strategies and reinforcement-based approaches.Background or coursework in psychology, behavioral science, child development, education, or a related field preferred.High school diploma or equivalent required; bachelor’s degree is required.Ability to follow clinical guidance, collaborate within a multidisciplinary team, and maintain confidentiality and professional boundaries.Comfort with active, hands-on work in community and home settings and the ability to provide physical assistance when required by an individual's support plan.Experience supporting neurodivergent individuals or individuals with developmental disabilities is strongly preferred; Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) certification is a plus.Reliable transportation and the ability to travel to client homes and community-based locations within assigned service areas are required. Come Grow With Bright MindsWe’re looking for compassionate, dependable, and motivated individuals who are excited to make a meaningful difference. If you’re passionate about helping others build confidence, develop independence, and strengthen skills for everyday life, we’d love to hear from you. Have questions about the position or what it’s like to work with Bright Minds? Reach out — we’d be happy to connect, answer your questions, and tell you more about our team. We look forward to meeting you and hopefully welcoming you to the Bright Minds team!

jobs.description: Employer: KinderCare Learning Companies Expires: 10/25/2026 Futures start here. Where first steps, new friendships, and confident learners are born. jobs.title: Infant Early Childhood Mental Health Consultant Contractor at Frost HR Consulting
jobs.description: Employer: Frost HR Consulting Expires: 10/25/2026 Multi-Region Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health ConsultantIndependent Contractor | Full-time | Oregon-based | Regular statewide travel requiredWhy This Work MattersThe earliest relationships shape lifelong well-being. At ORIMHA, we support the professionals who support infants, toddlers, and families across Oregon. This role helps expand access to Infant and Early Childhood Mental Health Consultation across the state, filling regional gaps and helping ensure early childhood educators, children, and families can access support when and where it is needed.About ORIMHAThe Oregon Infant Mental Health Association (ORIMHA) is a statewide nonprofit dedicated to supporting the emotional health and well-being of Oregon’s infants, toddlers, and their families.We achieve this through a network of parents and professionals committed to advancing infant mental health principles across the state. Through Endorsement, Reflective Supervision, and training, we help build a connected, skilled, and thoughtful workforce across Oregon, grounded in infant mental health principles and committed to equity, relationships, and long-term impact.About the RoleInfant and Early Childhood Mental Health (IECMH) Consultation is an indirect, multilevel service in which consultants partner with the adults in young children’s lives to build their capacity to foster healthy social-emotional development.In Every Child Belongs, consultants partner with early childhood care and education educators in center- and home-based settings. IECMH Consultation requires the use of the Consultative Stance to build strong, collaborative, and supportive relationships with educators. IECMH Consultants also engage with families (when the need is for child-specific consultation) and connect educators with resources available in their region.The broad goal of Every Child Belongs is to reduce rates of suspension/expulsion from ECE settings, and more specifically to reduce disparities in the rates of suspension/expulsion, specifically race and disability status, for example. Therefore, this position will require a strong commitment to equity, anti-bias, and anti-racist practices. Culturally specific and culturally responsive services are important to the success of the program. Consultants whose race, ethnicity, culture, and/or language are representative of the community served are strongly encouraged to apply.The Multi-Region IECMH Consultant will serve many areas of the state to fill gaps in regional IECMH Consultant availability, e.g., if a regional IECMHC must take a leave of absence. Multi-Region IECMHC may partner with a regional IECMH Consultant on individual cases, where appropriate, to expand capacity or meet critical needs. The Multi-Region IECMHC will also pilot the use of telehealth/video conferencing to deliver IECMHC when time or circumstances prevent timely in-person delivery or to provide live, virtual coaching to an IECMHC. The Multi-Region IECMH Consultant will function as part of the ORIMHA team, under the supervision of the Executive Director with support from the Operations Director. Driving is required, and regular travel of up to 1000 miles per month is anticipated.What You Will DoWhen filling in for a regional IECMH Consultant:Providing relationship-based, preventive interventions to promote the mental health of infants and young children and address behaviors that put them at risk of suspension/expulsion from early learning and childcare settings.Supporting ongoing communication with educators about early relational health and/or developmental concerns related to infants and young children.Developing written intervention strategies and using a collaborative approach to assist educators with implementing strategies that promote infants’ and young children’s optimal social-emotional development.Prioritizing service delivery to programs with few or no other resources available for support.Becoming familiar with unique racial, cultural, linguistic, historical, and regional characteristics, including understanding the demographics of families and educators in the region.Documenting service delivery, in alignment with written guidance.Making referrals for children and their families to appropriate outside services, as necessary.When appropriate, providing group and individual training on overall social and emotional wellness, infant and early childhood development, trauma-informed care, attachment, self-care, and other related topics.Additional responsibilities include:Piloting the use of telehealth/video conferencing to deliver IECMHC, when needed.Responding to requests for IECMH Consultation that are submitted by parents or professionals other than educators.Using independent judgment and discretion in practice in the field and in setting daily priorities to complete tasks.Demonstrating humility and sensitivity to racial, linguistic, cultural, social, economic, individual, and role differences between consultant and educator and between educator and the infant/young child & family.Bringing observations and questions to reflective supervision and engaging in the reflective process.Adhering to all data and program requirements.What You BringEducationMaster’s degree (mental health, early childhood education, early childhood development, physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, or other related discipline).If the Master’s degree is not from a mental health-related discipline, participation in mental health in-service training is preferred (as verified by existing Endorsement as Family Specialist – see below under Credential).CredentialEndorsed (IMH-E® or ECMH-E®) as Family Specialist or Mental Health Specialist or meets criteria for one of these categories of Endorsement.Preference for applicants who have also earned the Endorsed Reflective Supervisor add-on.ExperienceA minimum of two years of experience as an IECMH Consultant in early education settings.Preference for those who have used distance technology to deliver IECMH consultation.LocationTravel within the state of Oregon will be required to perform in-person work. Required SkillsCapacity for humility, empathy, curiosity, and flexibility.Ability to work at multiple levels (programmatic, groups, and individuals; educators, families, infants, and children).Effective communication skills (verbal and written).Comfort and skill in engaging in conversations about racism, bias, and equity.Capacity to foster strong professional relationships.Driving/ability to travel.Use of distance technology.Capacity to partner with and support other IECMH Consultants and partner organizations.Effective family engagement.Contractor Compensation & Additional InformationCompensation: $52.00 - 57.00/hrThis is an independent contractor position and is not eligible for ORIMHA employee benefits, including medical or dental insurance, retirement benefits, or paid time off. Must maintain insurance coverage required under the independent contractor agreement. Specific insurance requirements will be provided as part of the contracting process.Regular statewide travel is required, with travel of up to 1,000 miles per month anticipated.Approved business travel expenses, including mileage, will be reimbursed in accordance with ORIMHA guidelinesExpected contract term — June 2028Expected weekly hours/workload — 40Final candidates will be required to complete a background check, consistent with our commitment to supporting children, families, and communities we serve.ORIMHA is committed to equity, inclusion, and belonging in both our work and our hiring practices. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences, and we recognize the value of lived experience in strengthening our work. We strive to create a workplace where all individuals feel respected, supported, and able to contribute fully.
